title: Former UAE cyclist Cristian Camilo Munoz dies following medical complications six days after crash
content:
Former UAE Team Emirates rider Cristian Camilo Munoz has died following medical complications six days after a crash at the Tour de Jura in France.

The 30-year-old had been riding for Nu Colombia in the French one-day race on Saturday but could not finish after coming off his bike.

The Continental cycling team announced his death on their social media on Friday, with the Colombian Cycling Federation releasing a statement citing “medical complications” after Munoz’s crash as the cause of death.

The Colombian’s team-mates subsequently pulled out of the stage of the Vuelta Asturias Julio Alvarez Mendo due to take place that day.

“Today we say goodbye to Cristian Munoz, a cyclist who turned every kilometre into a testament to passion, discipline and heart,” the Nu Colombia statement said. “His story does not end here, and it reminds us that dreams are pedalled every day, even when the road gets tough.

“We are left with his example, his achieved goals and the inspiration he left in everyone who saw him get on his bike. To his family, friends and all those who admired him from near or far, we send all our strength and love at this time.”

The national federation also paid tribute on Friday.

“His passing leaves a huge void in Colombian cycling and in the hearts of all those who had the privilege of knowing him and sharing the road and races with him,” the statement read. “Cristian will be remembered for his dedication, discipline, and character both on and off the bike.”

Munoz started World Tour racing in 2019 with UAE, and stayed with the team — which included four-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar and Brandon McNulty — until 2021 when he moved to Colombian team EPM-Scott.

Munoz’s achievements included a stage win in the Giro Ciclistico d’Italia in 2018 and fourth place in the Colombia national championships in 2024.
